summary_paragraph: A male patient with cryptogenic cirrhosis was admitted for acute right-sided abdominal pain and distension. Initial concern for portal vein thrombosis was ruled out by CT despite a concerning ultrasound. Abdominal pain resolved with symptom management, and evaluation revealed no infectious cause. The distension was attributed to excess gas from high-dose lactulose. Hyponatremia developed during admission but corrected with fluid restriction. The patient remained encephalopathy-free and was discharged home with adjusted lactulose dosing, addition of rifaximin and ursodiol, and discontinuation of hydroxyzine. A renal hypodensity was noted on CT, prompting recommendation for follow-up ultrasound in six months. Outpatient follow-up with his liver specialist was arranged.
problems: Cirrhosis of liver without mention of alcohol
Diaphragmatic hernia without mention of obstruction or gangrene
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of prostate
